newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline rises on supply tightness.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline rises on supply tightness.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices defied a lower NYMEX late Monday and rose on trader talk of falling regional supplies.
Gasoline production problems at two major Los Angeles refineries and a third San Francisco plant lifted sellers prices, traders said.
"They're not at full production," a broker said, noting fires last month at Mobil's Torrance coker and Texaco's Wilmington hydrotreater still crimped output.
Rumors of equipment problems with Chevron's Richmond, Calif. fluid catalytic cracker, added to trader fears.
For the week ended November 29, refinery output fell 5.6 percent on the West Coast to 84.9 percent of capacity, according to data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Traders said Unocal would likely run a 35.5 degree API gravity Rincon crude at its Rodeo, Calif., plant to make lube products. The company purchased a 12,000 bpd term contract of the crude last week.
Bids for Los Angeles conventional grade gasoline rose 1.50 cents from the morning to 68.50 cents a gallon on increasing worries of supply tightness.
CARB gasoline rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 70/71 cents.
